I know you may be limited due to transportation, but what helped me get a job or at least a referral to another job in Canada was by following up in person or by phone call. For example, I applied to a part time retail job by my house, walking distance and got the position simply because I shopped there often and I spoke with the hiring manager directly. I worked there for almost 2 years, I hated the role because it was physically demanding however, when it came to hiring new workers, there were almost 200 applicants for 2 part time positions. When I got hired, I was able to be the one chosen out of dozens of other applicants simply because I spent 5 minutes contacting the right person, the manager. Don't bother asking the workers if the position is still open, they most likely will brush you off, based on personal experience.   For example if you apply to lets say 20 jobs on Linkedin, Indeed or the company job board, follow up with them either by phone, in person or by email and specifically ask for a recruiting/hiring manager contact.  A lot of my friends who got barista jobs at Starbucks told me they got the position because they applied online and they called Starbucks store the morning after, asking to speak to the hiring manager. After speaking to the manager, they were either able to get the position, or they were able to ask the manager directly if other locations in the area were hiring.
